title: Desktop Icons for Windows and Mac | Icons8
meta_description: Browse desktop icons in various styles and sizes. Find PNG and SVG files for folders, apps, and system shortcuts to organize your workspace.
intro: Organize your computer screen with icons designed for desktop environments. Choose from different visual styles and file formats to match your operating system and personal preference.

sections.heading: Styles for Different Workflows
paragraphs: Select a visual style that fits your screen layout, from flat and minimal designs to 3D and hand-drawn illustrations. Some styles work best for professional setups, while others add a playful touch to personal devices. The choice depends on whether you need icons to blend in or stand out against your wallpaper.

sections.heading: File Formats and Sizes
paragraphs: Desktop icons are available in standard image formats like PNG and scalable vector formats like SVG. PNG files are ready for immediate use on most operating systems, while SVG files allow you to resize the icon without losing quality. Check the specific dimensions listed for each asset to ensure it fits your folder or shortcut requirements.

sections.heading: Categories for Organization
paragraphs: Find specific symbols for common desktop tasks, including folders, applications, and system utilities. You can search for icons representing documents, media players, or network connections to create a logical structure on your screen. Grouping similar items with matching icons helps you locate files faster.

faq.question: What are the best file formats for desktop icons?
faq.answer: PNG is the most common format for desktop icons on Windows and Mac, while SVG is ideal if you need to resize the image frequently.

faq.question: Can I use these icons for personal desktops?
faq.answer: Yes, you can use these icons to organize your personal computer screen, but always check the license terms shown with each asset.

faq.question: Do these icons work on both Windows and Mac?
faq.answer: Most icons are designed to be compatible with both operating systems, provided you select the correct file format and size.

faq.question: How do I change a desktop icon?
faq.answer: Right-click the shortcut or folder, select properties, and choose the option to change the icon to browse for your new file.

faq.question: Are there icons for specific applications?
faq.answer: You can find icons representing common software categories like browsers, editors, and media players to label your shortcuts.
